title: Postmortem-to-QBR Bridge Playbook
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a compact playbook for turning a recent customer-facing postmortem into an actionable QBR agenda that directly influences renewal conversations. Use when an incident, onboarding failure, or delivery gap created renewed churn risk or opened opportunities for strategic remediation.

Why this exists (notes to self):
- We frequently run separate postmortems and QBRs; outcomes often don't translate into the customer-facing narrative.
- This doc forces a handoff: technical root cause -> customer impact -> remediation plan -> measurable milestone commitments we can present at QBR.
- Ideal for accounts with medium-to-high ARR and recent reliability or delivery issues.

When to use:
- Incident with customer-visible downtime in last 90 days
- Onboarding delay that missed SLA or milestone
- Repeated support escalations that map to product gaps

Quick workflow (30–90m prep):
1) Gather artifacts (owner: CSM) — postmortem doc, timeline, primary RCA bullets, customer-facing timeline of events, support tickets referenced.
2) Rapid impact distillation (owner: solutions engineer) — 3 bullets: what happened, customer-visible consequence, immediate mitigation taken.
3) Draft QBR agenda slice (owner: CSM) — 10–15 min slot to present incident + proposed remediation milestones.
4) Align internal stakeholders (owner: CSM lead) — SLA owner, Product PM, Eng incident lead, Solutions. Confirm on one slide and on proposed dates.
5) Rehearse facilitation script (10–20m) — who says what, accountability statements, ask of the customer.

One-slide narrative (40–60 seconds each section):
- Headline: 1-sentence summary and current ask ("We experienced X on DATE; impact was Y; here's what we've done and what we propose to prevent recurrence — we want alignment on timeline and escalation path").
- Timeline: 3 bullet timeline of incident and mitigations (T-0, T+mitigation, T+long-term fix planned).
- Impact metrics: uptime hours lost, affected features, estimated user-exposure, customer business impact (revenue, operations).
- Short-term mitigation (owner + completion ETA).
- Long-term fix (owner, milestone dates, risk level).
- How we’ll measure success (3 signals) and where the customer can observe progress.

Sample QBR agenda (30–60 min segment inside existing QBR):
- 00:00–02:00 Welcome + objectives (CSM)
- 02:00–07:00 Account health snapshot (usage, adoption, NPS)
- 07:00–20:00 Incident recap & impact narrative (SE + Eng lead)
- 20:00–30:00 Proposed remediation plan & milestones (Product + Eng)
- 30:00–35:00 Resource/priority ask and decision (CSM)
- 35:00–45:00 Risk-to-renewal and next steps (CSM + Customer)
- Remaining time: open Q&A and alignment on follow-ups

Facilitation script (concise lines to use):
- CSM open: "Thanks for the time — we want to be transparent about an event you experienced and share our concrete plan to ensure it won't recur. We also want your input on the proposed timeline so we can prioritize appropriately."

- SE incident summary: "On DATE at TIME, we observed X in the Y service which impacted Z customers for N minutes. The immediate remediation was A which restored baseline service. Importantly, we tracked the user impact — here are the numbers."

- Eng/RCA: "Prelim RCA shows root cause is P (brief). The long-term change we are planning is Q; the key milestones are M1 (P0), M2 (testing), M3 (deploy). We own M1 by DATE, M2 by DATE."

- CSM customer ask: "To give us runway for prioritized execution, we're asking for [prioritization / temporary exceptions / access] and your approval for the timeline. If you prefer a faster timeline, we can propose a dedicated engineering slot at cost."

- Close: "We will follow up with a one-page status update weekly until the long-term fix is shipped. If anything changes, your designated contacts will receive immediate updates."

Meeting prep checklist (CSM owner column) — copy to meeting prep doc and Slack thread:
- [ ] Insert one-slide narrative into QBR deck (owner: CSM)
- [ ] Attach postmortem link and top-5 timeline bullets for execs (owner: SE)
- [ ] Confirm attendance from Eng lead, Product PM, Solutions (owner: CSM)
- [ ] Pre-call with Eng lead to rehearse language and handoffs (owner: CSM)
- [ ] Prepare compensation/credits proposal scenario (owner: CSM + Finance)
- [ ] Update risk-to-renew scoring (see method below) (owner: CSM)
- [ ] Draft follow-up cadence (weekly one-pager + monthly checkpoint) (owner: CSM)
- [ ] Share Slack pre-read 24h before QBR (owner: CSM)

Risk-to-renew scoring (quick rubric):
- Red (High): incident caused >5% revenue impact, or core feature unusable, or executive-level escalation open.
- Amber (Medium): repeated user-level incidents, SLA breach but mitigated, customer unhappy but no exec escalation.
- Green (Low): single, short incident with negligible business impact and clear fix timeline.

Renewal tracker snippet (to paste into account sheet):
- Renewal risk: Red/Amber/Green
- Incident date: DATE
- Short description: 1-sentence
- Current mitigation status: immediate/underway/planned
- Long-term ETA: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner(s): list names
- Next update: YYYY-MM-DD

Customer-facing follow-up cadence (recommended):
- Immediate (within 48h): one-page incident summary + short-term mitigation completed.
- Weekly: 1-page status update that maps to milestones.
- Post-ship: 30/60/90 day check-ins to show stability metrics and adoption progress.

Negotiation and credits guidance (notes):
- Avoid promising credits in QBR; instead propose an options menu (tiered credits based on SLA miss + remediation speed).
- Have Finance sign-off before offering monetary credits.
- Offer technical remediation and operational guarantees as alternatives to credits (e.g., dedicated support, monitoring integration).

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- CSM: orchestrates narrative, facilitates decisions, owns renewal ask.
- SE: summarizes customer impact and customer-facing timeline.
- Eng lead/RCA owner: explains root cause, owns technical milestones.
- Product PM: owns prioritization tradeoffs and timeline commitments.
- Finance: approves any credits/compensation.

Post-QBR actions (immediately after meeting):
- Publish one-pager summary to customer + internal playbook link (owner: CSM)
- Create a progress board (light kanban) and invite customer to view (owner: SE)
- Set weekly sync invites and a standing owner for follow-ups (owner: CSM)
- Update renewal risk in CRM and notify renewals lead (owner: CSM)

Common pitfalls and mitigation (notes to self):
- Pitfall: engineering jargon overload. Mitigation: use "what happened" -> "customer impact" -> "what we will do" framing.
- Pitfall: committing to vague timelines. Mitigation: tie to milestones with owners and dates.
- Pitfall: surprises after QBR. Mitigation: commit to weekly updates; escalate changes immediately.

Appendix: quick templates to copy into slides or emails:
- One-line headline: "On DATE we experienced X; we have implemented A and will deliver B by DATE — weekly updates until B shipped."
- 48h email subject: "Incident summary and immediate mitigations — [Account]"
- Weekly status header: "Weekly status: milestone X (ETA), testing Y (ETA), blocker Z (if any)"

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Do we want a standardized credits formula in the global playbook? (action: escalate to Finance by NOV 20)
- Should the postmortem always generate a customer-facing summary? (action: propose to ops guild)
- Align a templated progress board format (action: SE + CSM to prototype)

References and links (placeholders):
- Postmortem template: CONFLUENCE:PMT-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
- Account tracker: SHEET:ACCT-TRACK-2025
- Example customer email: SLACK:DRAFTS/channel

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally light-weight and meant to be copy/paste ready. Feedback sought on: the risk rubric thresholds, whether credits guidance is too conservative, and how explicit we should be about asking for customer prioritization.

End of doc.
